label: Fires at late-episode D1 after a rewarded rare a1->S2 trial preceded by a rewarded trial.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1)
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial >= 90) * (tv("state", -2) == 1)
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (nonzero on 0.1% of steps), only at D1. Its magnitude is driven by a three-way conjunction: previous trial was a1 -> S2 (rare) rewarded, the trial before that was rewarded (mostly a1 -> S1), and the episode is in its last ~10 trials. Each part alone does little; the full conjunction carries most of the weight. In the free fit, belief_lo (the observer still leaning to S1) and the trial-before state being S1 add a bit more. The short form cannot write the 4-factor conjunction (phase x pattern x late x prior reward) as one term, so it approximates it with pairwise 3-factor terms; that is the main reason it falls short of the free fit. Many residual misses are activations on the first trial of a window, where the previous trial is not in view. Observed-only; no future or model-output terms.
